{"content":"# Mission: wave-2 E — work-first scenario creation (UX US 10)

Open ONE pull request on branch `feat/web-scenarios-work-first` targeting `main` — **issue #31 (PR body ends with `Closes #31`)**. Leave it open for
review; do not merge. Read `AGENTS.md` first, then both audits
(`docs/audits/2026-11-21-ux-audit.md`, `docs/audits/2026-11-21-ui-3d-audit.md`): you are
implementing **UX US 10 (finding F7)**. Wave-1 blocker #28 is merged — this mission is unblocked.
Presentation-only; **scenario payloads and the command vocabulary `building.*.update.v1` are
unchanged**: a scenario built through the new flow must produce byte-identical commands.

**File ownership (wave-2 rule, see `docs/ux/README.md`):** you own
`apps/web/src/components/ScenarioPanel.tsx` (the comparison table itself stays as-is — audit
says keep it; only its container adapts), a new work-catalog service (e.g.
`apps/web/src/services/work-catalog.ts`), and `tests/e2e/scenarios.spec.ts`. You may read but
must NOT modify B's `command-catalog.ts`, `services/enum-labels.ts`, `services/u-reading.ts`
or `hooks/use-enum-labels.ts` — reuse them by composition. Do NOT touch the editor dialog
(mission D owns `BuildingEditorPanel.tsx`), viewer files, or the API/domain.

## What to build

1. **Work-first creation flow (US 10 / F7)**: the scenario form starts from named renovation works
   — « Isolation des murs », « Isolation de la toiture », « Isolation du plancher »,
   « Remplacement des fenêtres », « Changement du chauffage », « Changement de la ventilation » —
   instead of raw command rows. Each work maps internally to its command type(s) from the existing
   catalog; the target element is picked by plain name and location (« Mur nord — 54 m² »: labeled
   kind + orientation label resolved through B's `use-enum-labels`/`enum-labels` service +
   area, with the raw id in secondary detail); numeric parameters reuse B's guided U reading
   (`describeU`); enum parameters reuse B's labeled selects (raw id still sent).
2. **Payloads byte-identical**: the composed commands are exactly what the current form produces
   (same `type`, same field keys, raw DPE enum ids, numeric U). Prove it in e2e: build the same
   scenario through the new flow and assert the scenario's command list matches the frozen payload
   field by field.
3. **Advanced mode**: the current command-row editor stays reachable behind an « avancé » toggle,
   with every existing `data-testid` preserved — the U-field-width regression of
   `scenarios.spec.ts` must keep passing without modification.
4. **Comparison table untouched**: rank, Δ kWh, Δ kg CO₂e, label change render exactly as today;
   do not restyle it beyond what the surrounding container requires.

## Constraints and quality bar

- Update `docs/user-guide.md` in the same PR — only the scenario section. Quoted labels must
  match the new UI literally (checked at review). Never edit another section.
- Tests: e2e covers the work-first flow end to end (create two scenarios through the new flow,
  compare) plus the byte-identity payload assertion; the pre-existing scenarios e2e keeps passing
  through the advanced mode. Unit tests for the work-mapping (work → command type(s), target-kind
  filtering, guided helpers).
- Run the app; before/after screenshots of the scenario form into `docs/audits/assets/`;
  reference them in the PR body.
- CI fully green (6 checks) on the PR head. PR body states which audit US/findings are closed
  (US 10 / F7) and anything deliberately left out (e.g. works without a matching catalog command).

{"content":"# User Guide — Home Energy Consumption Simulator

A short guide for homeowners using the web app (http://localhost:5173). The interface is in French, so UI labels are quoted in French below. Everything runs locally on your machine.

TODO: add screenshots of the import page, editor panel and comparison table when available.

## 1. Getting started

- Install Node 24.14.1 (pinned in `.nvmrc`) and start the app: see [local development](local-development.md). On Windows, `.\start-dev.ps1` does everything.
- Web app: http://localhost:5173 · API (for developers): http://localhost:3000, interactive documentation at `/docs`.

## 2. Import your DPE (XML)

1. On the home page (« Importer un DPE (XML) »), click **« Choisir un fichier DPE… »** and select your DPE file (`.xml`).
2. The file is imported in under a second. A success banner shows « Bâtiment importé : DPE <numéro du DPE> » (e.g. « DPE 2238E0097309E »), with the raw building id in small monospace next to it, and the **workspace** opens on the **« Synthèse »** tab. Four tabs organize the building: **« Synthèse »**, **« Rapport d'import »**, **« Éditeur du bâtiment »**, **« Scénarios de rénovation »**. The workspace header always shows the primary action **« Lancer la simulation »** and the link **« Voir le modèle 3D »**. The « Synthèse » tab shows the latest simulation summary at the top, plus the values that had to be estimated, marked « estimé — à vérifier »; the full field-by-field import report is in the **« Rapport d'import »** tab.
3. An invalid file shows an error banner and nothing is saved.

### Reading the import report

The report is a list of collapsible sections, each showing only its count in the header: **« Champs lus (n) »**, **« Champs inférés (n) »**, **« n chemins non reconnus »** and **« Champs absents (n) »**.

- Fields read directly from the DPE are **measured**.
- **« Champs inférés (n) »** are values the app had to assume (the DPE did not provide them). This section is open by default: each inferred value is a card showing the value, its provenance in plain words (**« mesuré par le DPE »** or **« estimé — à vérifier »**), its `confiance` score with a color (green ≥ 0.8, orange ≥ 0.5, red below) and its import date. Inferred values are never presented as certain.
- **« n chemins non reconnus »** folds the raw XML paths of the file into a count. Expand the section, then click **« Voir la liste des chemins »** to list them one by one, or **« Copier la liste »** / **« Télécharger le détail »** to keep the full list (copy or `.txt` file).
- **« Champs absents (n) »** lists the missing fields with the reason why they are missing.

## 3. Run the energy simulation

1. **« Lancer la simulation »** is the single primary button of the **workspace header** — always visible, whatever tab you are on.
2. The latest result summary appears at the **top of the « Synthèse » tab**: the **energy label** (« Énergie : X ») and **climate label** (« Climat : X »), the consumption `n kWh/m².an`, emissions `n kg CO₂/m².an`, the totals in kWh and kg CO₂e, and the engine version (« moteur Open3CL v… »).
3. In the same tab, the panel « Simulation énergétique (Open3CL) » keeps the technical detail behind expanders: the **history** (« Historique (n) ») and the raw engine output (« Voir la sortie brute du moteur », opt-in).
4. Each run is saved in the building's **history**. Running again on an unchanged building instantly returns the cached result — no recalculation (a « résultat servi depuis le cache » badge appears in the header).

## 4. What the numbers mean

- **kWh/m².an** — the dwelling's yearly energy consumption per square meter (all 5 regulated uses: heating, hot water, cooling, lighting, auxiliaries). Lower is better.
- **kg CO₂e/m².an** — yearly greenhouse-gas emissions per square meter.
- **Labels A–G** — the regulatory DPE scale: **A** is the most efficient, **G** the least. « Énergie » is the energy label, « Climat » the emissions (GES) label. A renovation usually moves both (e.g. **D → C**).

## 5. Edit the building (P4 editor) — golden path

The panel « Éditeur du bâtiment (2D) » lets you change the dwelling and see the impact immediately. Each element row tells you in plain words where its value comes from — **« mesuré par le DPE »**, **« estimé — à vérifier »** or **« saisi par vous »** — with the numeric score as a subtle secondary indicator and the raw source path behind **« d'où vient cette valeur ? »**; the **« Synthèse »** tab aggregates all the estimated values in one place.

1. In the element list, click **« Modifier »** on an element (e.g. a wall).
2. Change a value in the dialog, e.g. the wall's **U (W/m².K)** — a lower U means better insulation. Click **« Enregistrer »**.
3. The dialog works in **plain language**: enum fields (orientation, type de mur, vitrage…) are labeled lists — pick « Nord » or « murs en béton banché », the raw DPE id is shown as secondary information and is exactly what gets sent. U fields keep a numeric input bounded to **0–4 W/m².K**, with a plain-language reading of the current or typed value (« mur non isolé », « isolation moyenne », « très bonne isolation ») and an example in the helper text. The « **Afficher les valeurs techniques** » toggle reveals the raw ids/values exactly as they will be sent. An **invalid value** (e.g. negative U) is rejected right in the field with a message in plain French (« U doit être compris entre 0 et 4 W/m².K » — the raw technical message stays available in the « Message technique » expander); nothing is saved and the version does not change.
4. On **save** (only the display changed — the command sent to the server still carries the raw values): the building version increases (shown as « version N »), and an **« Impact du dernier changement »** summary appears right in the editor panel — « Simulation relancée : −X kWh/an, étiquette D → C » (the CO₂ delta is added when it changes; when the label does not move, it honestly says « étiquette D inchangé »), followed by a plain-language diff of what the command changed (« U du mur wall-1 : 1,64 → 0,20 », with a French decimal comma). A **new simulation runs automatically** — the consumption and labels update (on the sample fixture, insulating a wall U 1,64 → 0,20 moves the label D → C). The raw trail stays available in the **« Piste d'audit (détail technique) »** expander (old → new value, marked `[user, confiance 1]`).
5. If someone else saved changes in between, your save is refused with **409** and the panel shows « Conflit de version : le bâtiment a été modifié ailleurs. État rechargé (version N), réessayez. » — the panel reloads the current state; just redo your edit and save again.
6. **« Annuler le dernier changement »** undoes the last edit: it restores the previous value *with its original provenance* (the DPE value, not a user value), is itself recorded in the audit trail, and the displayed simulation result is refreshed — usually straight from the cache, since the restored building hashes back to the original input.

TODO: screenshot of the editor dialog with a field error, and of the audit trail.

## 6. Compare renovation scenarios (P5) — golden path

The panel « Scénarios de rénovation » lets you price several renovation packages before doing any work.

1. Create a scenario: under **« Nouveau scénario »**, give it a name + description (e.g. « Isolation des murs »), then describe the planned work under **« Travaux envisagés »**: pick a **« Travail »** (« Isolation des murs », « Isolation de la toiture », « Isolation du plancher », « Remplacement des fenêtres », « Changement du chauffage », « Changement de la ventilation »), then the **« Élément »** concerned — shown by plain name and location, e.g. « Mur nord — 54,25 m² » (the raw element id stays visible in small text) — then the performance level, e.g. U = 0.2 W/m².K in the **« U (W/m².K) »** field, with a plain-language reading of the value (e.g. « très bonne isolation »). Click **« Ajouter un travail »** to add more works to the same scenario, then **« Créer le scénario »**. The scenario appears in the list. (The raw command editor is still available behind **« Mode avancé »**.)
2. Click **« Simuler »** on a scenario: it is simulated through the same regulatory engine as the current building.
3. Click **« Comparer les scénarios »**: a table appears with the current state pinned as **« État initial »**, and one row per scenario with its absolute consumption/emissions, its labels, the **deltas vs the current state** in kWh and in kg CO₂e (negative = savings), the **« Changement d'étiquette »** (e.g. « D → C »), and its **« Rang »** (1 = the scenario saving the most kWh). Comparing again from cache takes well under a second.
4. Click **« Appliquer »** on a scenario to apply it to the building: the building state changes, the change is written to the audit trail, the version increases, and the current state is re-simulated.
5. Deleting a scenario only removes the scenario and its links — the building and its simulation results are never deleted.

TODO: screenshot of the comparison table.

## 7. The 3D model (P3)

Click **« Voir le modèle 3D »** after an import — that is the entry point. (Fallback: open the route `#/building/<buildingId>` directly, using the id shown in the « Bâtiment importé » banner.) The header shows the **DPE number** of the diagnostic (the internal id appears in small monospace text under the title). The dwelling is shown upright on its plot, in a default 3/4 view; orbit/zoom around it (the camera cannot go under the ground). Click an element to see its properties in the side panel (id, type, label, area, U-value, orientation, placement). Each value is annotated in plain words — **mesuré par le DPE** vs **estimé — à vérifier** (or **saisi par vous** for a value you entered yourself) — with the confidence score as a subtle secondary indicator and the raw source path behind **« d'où vient cette valeur ? »**; the element itself carries a chip telling whether it came straight from the DPE or was inferred; the selection is highlighted with an outline. On hover, a tooltip shows the element's `{ source, confidence }` (and its share of total losses in % when the heat-loss overlay is on). Elements whose geometry was inferred carry a subtle hatch, also listed in the legend. Room names are shown as labels over the model — toggle them with **« Étiquettes des pièces »**. Once a simulation has run, switch on **« Pertes de chaleur »**: the legend is a gradient from **0 %** to **part max** (the worst element of this run is red), so the colors always span the full scale.

## 8. For developers

The REST API is documented interactively at http://localhost:3000/docs (OpenAPI): import, buildings, geometry, simulations and jobs, editing (`PATCH /buildings/:id` with `If-Match`, audit, undo), scenarios (create, simulate, compare, apply, delete). All energy figures come from the Open3CL engine only — the app never computes energy itself.

# Issue #48 — Level S validation findings: feasibility analysis & plan (DECISION ONLY, nothing implemented)

## 1. Feasibility analysis (grounded in the codebase)

**Files read:** `harness-poc/tasks/issue-48-level-s-validat.md` (matches live GitHub issue #48 in `P-Bouche/home-energy-consumption-simulator`, state: open), `apps/web/src/services/u-reading.ts`, `apps/web/test/u-reading.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/components/BuildingEditorPanel.tsx`, `apps/web/src/components/ScenarioPanel.tsx`, `apps/web/src/components/command-catalog.ts`, `apps/web/src/services/work-catalog.ts`, `apps/web/src/services/error-messages.ts`, `apps/web/src/store/editor-store.ts`, `packages/domain/src/commands.ts`, `tests/e2e/building-editor.spec.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`, `docs/audits/2026-11-21-ux-audit.md`, `docs/ux/wave1-B-editor-plain-language.md`, `docs/ux/wave2-E-scenarios-work-first.md`, `docs/user-guide.md`.

**Finding 1 (Uw > 4 via manual input) — CONFIRMED.** There is no literal MUI `Slider` in the current code; the "slider" of the audit (`docs/audits/2026-11-21-ux-audit.md`, F1: "slider with a sane range + numeric fallback") was implemented as a `type="number"` input whose clamp is only the HTML `min`/`max` attributes (`BuildingEditorPanel.tsx:395-399`, `min: 0, max: 4` in the `KINDS` field defs). HTML min/max do not block typed input, and `onSave` (`BuildingEditorPanel.tsx:236-256`) only checks `Number.isNaN` before putting the raw number into the command — no range check. So typing `5` is sent verbatim in the PATCH and only rejected afterwards by the domain (`packages/domain/src/commands.ts`, `U_VALUE_MAX = 4` in `validateCommandFields`), surfacing as a 400 translated by `error-messages.ts`. Note: e2e `tests/e2e/building-editor.spec.ts` AC-P4-02 currently *asserts* the raw invalid value (`uValueWm2K: -1`) is sent — any client-side clamp/block changes that test. Same gap exists in the scenario path (`command-catalog.ts` `buildCommand`, only NaN-checked; catalog carries min/max as presentation data only).

**Findings 2–3 (illogical U readings) — DECOMPOSES INTO ONE REAL BUG + ONE DESIGN QUESTION.**
- Real bug: in `BuildingEditorPanel.tsx:375-381`, `effective = Number.isFinite(typedNum) && typedNum > 0 ? typedNum : Number(current)` — when the user types `0` (or a negative), the reading silently falls back to the *stored* value's reading. That exactly reproduces "Uw 0 → baie vitrée non isolée" when the stored Uw > 1.5. (`u-reading.ts` itself is correct: `uBand(0)` → `null`, `describeU(0)` → `''`, covered by `apps/web/test/u-reading.test.ts`.) The scenario panel does it differently (`ScenarioPanel.tsx` `renderCatalogField`: typed 0 → no reading at all) — an inconsistency between the two surfaces.
- Design question: Uw 2, 3, 4 → "non isolée" is *by design* of the single shared band table in `u-reading.ts` (U > 1.5 → `non-isole`), which the wave-1 B mission doc states as the chosen thresholds. Whether windows need their own thresholds (the audit's level-M vocabulary: simple/double/double récent/triple vitrage mapped to Uw) is a product decision, not a code bug. Walls ("pareil pour mur") use the same shared table — the wall symptom is the same 0/negative fallback bug, not inverted thresholds.

**Findings 4–5 (Sw, q4pa unexplained) — CONFIRMED, pure gap.** In `BuildingEditorPanel.tsx` `KINDS`, `solarFactorSw` (window) and `q4paConv` (ventilation-system) have no `helper`/`uNoun` — unlike every U field. Validation *messages* for them are already translated (`error-messages.ts` `FIELD_SUBJECTS`: "Le facteur solaire Sw", "q4pa conv"), but there is no proactive plain-language reading. Domain ranges exist to mirror: Sw ∈ [0, 1], q4pa ∈ [0, 3] m³/(h.m²) (`commands.ts`). The UX vocabulary source is `docs/audits/2026-11-21-ux-audit.md` + `docs/user-guide.md`; no Sw/q4pa thresholds exist anywhere in the repo yet.

**Boundary check:** all five findings live in `apps/web` (presentation/validation). The domain contract (`building.*.update.v1`, `U_VALUE_MAX`, ranges) stays frozen and remains the enforcing layer — consistent with the issue's constraint and AGENTS.md §4 (no engine math). Test infra is ready: Vitest picks up `apps/*/test/**/*.test.ts` with 80 % coverage thresholds (`vitest.config.ts`); e2e is Playwright (`tests/e2e/building-editor.spec.ts`).
